## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Northern-Sòng re-translation by **Dānapāla** ([施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7)) of the *thousand-turning Avalokiteśvara dhāraṇī* tradition that Zhìtōng [智通](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%80%9A) had translated in 653 ([KR6j0233](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0233) T1035). Dānapāla's version is conducted from a freshly-imported Sanskrit manuscript at the Northern-Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* 譯經院 and represents a recension distinct from Zhìtōng's earlier translation.

**Abstract**

Dānapāla's late-tenth / early-eleventh-century translation of the *Qiānzhuǎn dàmíng tuóluóní* updates the Tang-period vocabulary of [KR6j0233](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0233) to the Northern-Sòng standard transliteration norms (which by the late tenth century used **Siddham** Sanskrit script and a more philologically-precise *fǎnqiè* phonetic apparatus). The two recensions — Zhìtōng (Tang, 653) and Dānapāla (Sòng, ca. 990) — together document the centuries-long evolution of the *Qiānzhuǎn* dhāraṇī tradition in Chinese transmission.
